_meta.status: TEMPLATE — every url below is a PLACEHOLDER CANDIDATE. None has been verified.
integrity_warnings: Government and grid-operator publication URLs change constantly and are frequently restructured without redirects. DO NOT trust any URL in this file. Discover the current URL at build time (ticket C-T03), verify it resolves, record its sha256, and store the retrieval timestamp.
Never hard-code a URL from memory or from an LLM's answer. The retrieval layer must re-discover at runtime via Tavily and validate before ingesting.
Most of these documents are Dutch. Preserve original-language quotes verbatim and provide your own translation alongside, marked as yours. Never present a translation as a quotation.

Check the licence/publication terms of each source before redistributing extracted text in an Apache-2.0 repo. Dutch government publications are frequently CC0 or under a public-data licence, but DSO and TenneT publications may have their own terms — record what you find in docs/DATA-SOURCES.md.
Grid-operator names, logos and letterheads must NOT be reproduced as branding in the UI or video. Naming them in a text citation is fine and necessary; using their logo is not.

must_include: at least one DSO congestion register
at least one DSO indicative forecast (codeerprognose)
at least one national regulator decision on the congestion-management framework
at least one national or sector overview of where congestion exists
required_document_set.target_coverage: every DSO in NL, plus at least one non-Dutch region as a stretch

document_families.role: PRIMARY — establishes whether congestion is registered for an area, and in which direction
document_families.why_it_matters: This is the authoritative statement of 'is there capacity here, in this direction'. Everything downstream depends on it.
expected_publishers: the four/five Dutch distribution system operators (DSOs / netbeheerders)
candidate_urls: TODO_DISCOVER — search: '<DSO name> congestieregister 2026', '<DSO name> netcongestie kaart'
TODO_DISCOVER — the sector portal that aggregates DSO congestion information
discovery_queries_nl: waar is congestie op het elektriciteitsnet
discovery_queries_en: electricity grid capacity map Netherlands by postcode
expected_fields: available capacity in kW or MW
document_families.extraction_difficulty: MEDIUM–HIGH — frequently a map or a spreadsheet rather than text; may require XLSX or GeoJSON parsing rather than PDF extraction
document_families.notes: Start with the operator for your own region (Brabant/Eindhoven). Getting one operator end-to-end is worth more than five half-ingested.

document_families.role: PRIMARY — the indicative, explicitly NON-BINDING forecast of when capacity returns
document_families.why_it_matters: This is the document everyone wants and everyone misreads. It contains the date, and it contains the language saying the date is not a promise.
candidate_urls: TODO_DISCOVER — search: 'codeerprognose <DSO name>', 'prognose netcongestie', 'verwachting capaciteit teruglevering'
discovery_queries_nl: prognose wanneer komt er capaciteit terug
document_families.extraction_difficulty: MEDIUM — the date is usually explicit, but the BINDING LANGUAGE is the hard part
document_families.critical_extraction_note: You MUST extract the document's own wording about binding status. Look for terms indicating non-binding/indicative/subject to change. If the document does not say, set binding='unknown' — NEVER default to 'binding'. This single rule is insight #2 and the reason the gate exists.
document_families.revision_tracking: HIGH PRIORITY — extract any self-reported version history (v2 → v3, previous indication X → now Y). These become RevisionEvents with source='document_self_reported' and are publishable on day one.

document_families.why_it_matters: Explains why the local answer is what it is, and provides the national numbers for the Impact story

document_families.role: RULES — what operators are allowed to offer, and what a requester is entitled to
document_families.why_it_matters: This is where the non-firm connection, flexibility arrangements and congestion-management participation come from. Insight #3's legal basis.
candidate_urls: TODO_DISCOVER — search: '<regulator> besluit congestiemanagement', 'kader congestiemanagement', 'besluit niet-firma aansluiting'

what operators must offer when congested

document_families.notes: Cache this heavily: it changes slowly but it is referenced by every single answer. This is the biggest cached-token win in the project.
